abstract: One-step image editors enable search over alternative prompts and random seeds, but using these candidates effectively requires balancing edit fidelity, source preservation, and computation. We present SearchChord, a training-free framework that combines text-based preselection, optional image verification, and latent-field recomposition. TextSim preselects ten of 100 candidates using text similarity, computes their control fields, and optionally reweights them using image-verifier scores. Experiments on PIE-Bench and CropWeed-EditBench reveal a consistent preservation–semantic trade-off: recomposition improves preservation of unchanged content, while candidate selection can achieve stronger target-text alignment. On PIE-Bench, diagnostic oracle recomposition reaches 24.73 dB PSNR, whereas oracle selection from 200 candidates reaches 25.46 CLIP-Edited. Practical verification partially recovers semantic alignment but does not eliminate the loss associated with recomposition, including on agricultural edits. These findings motivate text-first preselection and stronger verification to balance preservation, edit fidelity, and computational cost.
